sn45.11:2.2: In these reflections, the Buddha links the eightfold path with dependent origination, which he practiced after awakening ([ud1.1]()–3). Compare [dn1:3.45.1](), where he points out that wrong views are “conditioned by contact”, which is the immediately prior link of dependent origination.
sn45.11:2.4: We can apply this insight at multiple levels. For example, one with wrong view can get angry when right view is taught, which creates certain unpleasant feelings. More subtly, every mental state is associated with feeling, so when one is entertaining wrong view there is some kind of feeling there, perhaps a pleasant feeling arising from the idea that one knows the truth ([snp4.13]()). But the link with dependent origination also suggests something more long term: wrong view conditions rebirth. For pernicious wrong view—for example, the idea that there is no such thing as right and wrong—rebirth will be in lower realms, in which one will experience painful feelings.
